m2c/src/m2c/link/__init__.py -- Patch C04: the device link, this client's
WebSocket connection to the MiniMe server.

    client.py      ``DeviceLink``: handshake (hello with the device credential,
                   welcome, protocol check), run.start / run.resume, the
                   request table (ping/pong, error by ref_id), keepalive,
                   graceful shutdown, and the rule that every accepted server
                   event is appended to the session's event log exactly once and
                   in order (duplicates dropped, gaps never stored out of order)
    reconnect.py   the backoff (exponential, full jitter, capped, reset only by a
                   connection that stayed up), the error classes, and which
                   failures are final (unauthorized, device_revoked,
                   protocol_unsupported, superseded, store failure) versus
                   retried

Typical use::

    from m2c.link import DeviceLink, LinkCallbacks
    from m2c.store import open_db

    async with DeviceLink(open_db(), callbacks=LinkCallbacks(on_event=show)) as link:
        await link.wait_connected(10)
        run_id = await link.start_run(project_path=cwd, mode="ask",
                                      cwd_label="my-project", instructions=text)
        await link.send_user_message(run_id, "hello")
        ...

Executing tools is not here (C05 and later): ``tool_proposed`` events are stored
and handed to ``LinkCallbacks.on_tool_proposed``.

m2c/src/m2c/link/client.py -- Patch C04: the device link, the WebSocket
client that keeps this machine connected to the MiniMe server.

WHAT IT IS
----------
``DeviceLink`` is the one long-lived connection of build plan section 7 / P00
(protocol/README.md).  It does the plumbing so that the rest of the client can
think in runs and events:

* connects to ``wss://<server>/v1/code/device`` and says ``hello`` with the
  device credential (C03's ``load_credential()``); there is no JWT on the
  socket, the credential itself authenticates it.  It then insists on a valid
  ``welcome`` and refuses a server whose ``min_protocol`` is above anything
  this client speaks (``LinkProtocolUnsupportedError``);
* reconnects by itself with exponential backoff and full jitter
  (reconnect.py), stopping for good on ``unauthorized``, ``device_revoked``,
  ``protocol_unsupported`` and being superseded by a newer connection;
* after every (re)connect sends ``run.resume{last_seq}`` for each active run
  and keeps the local event log exactly equal to the server's stream: no
  duplicate, no missing, no out-of-order event (see below);
* correlates requests and answers (ping/pong by nonce, ``error`` by
  ``ref_id``) with timeouts, and runs an application-level keepalive;
* shuts down gracefully: ``aclose()`` closes the socket with a normal close
  frame, cancels every task it started and leaves the store consistent.

m2c/src/m2c/link/reconnect.py -- Patch C04: when to try again, how long to
wait, and which failures mean "stop for good".

The device link (client.py) holds one WebSocket to the server for as long as the
person is working.  Networks drop, laptops sleep, servers restart, so the link
reconnects by itself -- but a loop that keeps retrying a revoked device is a
bug, so this module also decides what ends the loop.

THE BACKOFF: exponential, FULL jitter, capped
---------------------------------------------
After the n-th failure in a row the next wait is drawn uniformly from
``[0, min(cap, base * factor**n))`` -- "full jitter".  The usual alternative,
"the delay plus a little noise", leaves many clients that were dropped by the
same server restart retrying in near lock-step; spreading each wait over the
whole interval spreads the herd.  Defaults: base 1 s, factor 2, cap 30 s.

The sequence is reset only by a connection that *actually stayed up*
(``stable_after_s``, 10 s by default).  A server that accepts the handshake and
drops the socket at once must not hold the delay at its minimum: that would be
a tight retry loop with extra steps.  A connect that never got as far as
``welcome`` has not stayed up either.

The random source and the clock are parameters (``Backoff(rng=...)``, and the
link's ``clock=``/``sleep=``), so tests are instant and exact.
